stem:
The diagram shows sun-heated land warming the moist air above a school playground. Siddharth watches the air rise and a dark cloud form before a thunderstorm begins.

Which claim correctly describes the chain that produces the thunderstorm?

options.text: Warm moist air rises over the heated land, leaving a low-pressure area; cooler air then flows in and the rising moist air forms the cloud.
Cool dry air sinks first over the heated land and that sinking alone forms the thunderstorm cloud.
Warm moist air need not rise; a thunderstorm cloud still forms over the heated land.
The dark cloud forms only because the cloud shape in the diagram looks dark.

teacher.key_rationale: Heated land warms moist air so it rises and leaves low pressure; cooler air flows in and the rising moist air builds the cloud. Cool dry air sinking first swaps the chain; skipping rise omits the needed condition; judging from paint colour is a surface feature.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote force-on-object diagram into heated land, rising moist air, and a cloud.
